You are an experienced NSW HSC Business Studies marker. Mark the student's response to a question from the 2018 NSW HSC Business Studies exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting.

Question 24(c) [5 marks]: A business has decided to expand into a larger factory and is now considering its financial options.
Discuss the use of leasing and the use of mortgages as a source of long-term finance for this business.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 5):
5 marks: Provides detailed points for and/or against the use of leasing and mortgages as a source of long-term finance
4 marks: Provides points for and/or against the use of leasing and mortgages as a source of long-term finance
3 marks: Provides characteristics and features of leasing and/or mortgages as a source of long-term finance
2 marks: Sketches in general terms leasing and/or mortgages
1 marks: Refers to leasing and/or mortgages

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
A mortgage could be used to purchase a factory. The business can use the new factory site as security and it has the advantage that it owns the property once the mortgage is fully repaid. It has the disadvantage that bank charges and interest have to be paid. The business may lease which is similar to renting the property. It does not pay for maintenance and the lease payments are tax deductible. It does not own the property at the end of the lease period.



WHAT THE REAL MARKERS SAID ABOUT THIS QUESTION:
Better responses: demonstrate what liquidity is and why it is an objective of financial management (a)
Better responses: demonstrate the ways a relevant strategy could improve the management of the accounts receivable turnover (b)
Better responses: provide clear and detailed advantages and disadvantages of using both leasing and mortgages (c).
To improve: providing reasons why liquidity is an objective – not just defining what liquidity is (a)
To improve: focusing on the ways a business could improve the accounts receivable turnover rather than providing characteristics and features of a strategy (b)
To improve: providing more than just a description of leasing and mortgages (c).

STUDENT RESPONSE:

Rules: the mark is an estimate against the listed criteria only; never invent criteria that are not listed. Quote the student's own words as evidence for every mark you award. If the response is too short, off topic or unreadable to judge, give the mark the criteria allow (usually 0 or 1), set confidence to "low" and say why in the verdict.

Return JSON only, no prose, in this exact shape:
{"mark": <integer 0-5>, "band": "<the criteria row it fits, e.g. '5'>", "verdict": "<one sentence saying why it got that mark>", "evidence": ["<up to 3 short quotes, under 15 words each, taken word for word from the student's response, that earned marks; [] if none>"], "strengths": ["<up to 3 short points>"], "missing": ["<up to 3 elements the criteria row above this one needs and the response lacks>"], "improvements": ["<up to 3 concrete things to add or change to reach the next row, each under 25 words>"], "next": "<the single most useful next action for this student, under 20 words>", "confidence": "<high, medium or low>", "model": "<a full-mark answer in 2 to 5 plain sentences a student could realistically write in the exam>"}
